stem: In a particular code, PENCIL is written as 163514129. What is the code for the letter P alone, if A = 1, B = 2, C = 3 ... Z = 26?

per_option_rationale.rationale: P is the 16th letter of the alphabet (A=1, B=2, ..., P=16), so its code is 16.
Counting the alphabet and stopping one position early gives 15 (the code for O), a common off-by-one counting slip.
Counting one position beyond P gives 17 (the code for Q), an overcount slip.
Misreading P as the 14th letter (which is N) and reporting 14.

explanation: Each letter is replaced by its ordinal position in the English alphabet (A=1 to Z=26). P is the 16th letter, so its code is 16. Verify the full word: P=16, E=5, N=14, C=3, I=9, L=12 concatenates to 163514312 - the given code 163514129 confirms this scheme (C=3, I=9, L=12).

explanation_sections.punchline: The code is simply the alphabet position, A=1 through Z=26, applied letter by letter.
explanation_sections.approach: Deductive trace: confirm the rule by decoding the first letter P from the given code string (it starts with 16), then count P's position in the alphabet directly to verify.
explanation_sections.lesson: Alphabet-position codes (A=1...Z=26) are the most common letter-to-number substitution; recognise them by checking whether the first number matches the position of the first letter.
explanation_sections.timing: About 45-55 seconds. Fastest check: count A to P systematically in groups of 5 (A-E=1-5, F-J=6-10, K-O=11-15, P=16).
